Hi Alex — great to hear. Thanks for the clear constraints; below is a concise operational primer that we can expand in the kickoff. Marissa (CS lead) will join the workshop and handle onboarding logistics.

High-level proposal (short):
- Pre-kickoff: share S3 manifest + representative query log (2–3k queries). Redwood will run a quick sample to estimate token distribution and embedding cost.
- Seed strategy (48-hr window): 1) Sample-based priming (10% stratified sample across doc age + traffic) to validate chunking and embed model; 2) Parallel backfill with sharded workers tuned to target 12–18 hour throughput to stay inside the window; 3) Live prefix/KV caching for hottest prefixes during the backfill to protect latency SLOs.
- Vector DB recommendation: For initial rollout we recommend using Redwood-managed vectorstore (hosted) with option to pin to Pinecone/Weaviate after acceptance. Hosted gives fastest iteration (snapshot + rollback) and reduced operational overhead.
- Chunking & embeddings: start with 512-token windows with 128-token overlap; default model: redwood-embed-medium. If median doc length permits, we can switch to 768 for better context coverage.
- Rerank smoke validation (what to measure): MRR@10, NDCG@10, relevancy precision@5, and 95th percentile latency for rerank path. Acceptance criteria: relative lift >= +8% MRR@10 vs current baseline and tail latency <= 120ms for rerank-only calls under expected QPS.
- Rollback & safety: run A/B on 10% traffic, monitor quality regressions with alerting to auto-fallback to baseline index.

Deliverables for kickoff (we'll produce these):
- Prime & backfill checklist (attached)
- Rerank smoke test matrix (we'll draft test cases and expected queries)
- Cost + footprint estimate (per-index token + storage) after sample run
- Mutual action plan with owners and dates

Proposed kickoff windows (PST): Tue 2026-12-22 10:00–11:30, Wed 2026-12-23 13:00–14:30, or Mon 2026-12-28 09:00–10:30. Which works best?

Adding a few engineering-level constraints and concrete acceptance checks for the smoke tests. I'm including these inline so we can lock the test plan in the workshop.

Operational notes:
- Backfill throughput: For 5.2M docs at avg 350 tokens (approx 1.82B tokens) and redwood-embed-medium (est 0.0004 USD/token) we should budget for ~USD 728 per full re-embed (ballpark; we'll run sample to refine). We can reduce cost by 30–45% using prefix caching + selective re-embed for unchanged docs.
- Chunking: 350 token avg -> 1 chunk per doc with 512-window acceptable; keep overlap small to reduce vector count. Expect ~5.5M vectors after chunking accounting for attachments and metadata.
- Storage: hosted vectorstore ~ 5.5M vectors * 1536 dims * 4 bytes ≈ 34GB raw; index overhead and metadata ~x2 => ~70GB.

Rerank smoke acceptance criteria (concrete):
- Evaluation set: 1k labeled queries (mix: navigational 40%, informational 50%, transactional 10%), each with top-10 judgment list.
- Metrics: baseline vs new rerank (MRR@10, NDCG@10, P@5). Pass if MRR@10 improves by >=0.08 absolute OR relative lift >=8% (we prefer absolute).
- Latency: end-to-end rerank median < 60ms, p95 < 120ms at expected staging QPS (we'll simulate expected qps provided by Searchly).
- QA/Smoke scenarios: cold-start search, heavy tail queries, and long-context queries (>1k tokens). I'll attach the workbook with test scenarios.

Rollback plan:
- Canary 10% traffic -> evaluate for 48h sliding window -> auto switch to baseline if MRR degradation > 3% or p95 latency > 150ms.

Engineering asks for kickoff prep:
- Provide sample S3 prefix (2–5k docs) + current query logs (anonymized).
- Provide current baseline eval dataset (if exists) or consent to Redwood building one from query logs.
- Confirm expected peak QPS for the 48-hour backfill period.

Forwarding R&D attachment: rerank-smoke-scenarios.xlsx (contains scenario matrix + synthetic load steps).

- Rishi
Senior Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
